advisor_identified: Albert Victor Tucker, historian of British history at York University’s Glendon College from 1966 and former principal of Glendon.

doctorate.title: Conservative transition in England: Disraeli to Mallock, 1867-1900

evidence.says: York University Archives identifies Albert Tucker as a history professor at Glendon from 1966 and principal in 1970–1975, and states that he earned his PhD at Harvard University.

York identifies the historian as Albert Victor Tucker, states that he pursued a PhD in British history at Harvard, joined York’s History Department in 1966, and taught at Glendon and in the Graduate Department of History until 1993.

Harvard’s catalogue names the author as Tucker, Albert Victor; gives the title Conservative transition in England: Disraeli to Mallock, 1867-1900; and states: “Thesis (Ph. D.)--Harvard University, 1958.”

notes: The catalogue’s full author name matches York’s identification, and its institution, year and title match linked AHA record 58577. Harvard catalogue metadata was read through its public LibraryCloud API: https://api.lib.harvard.edu/v2/items.json?recordIdentifier=990039923230203941.
